stories.title: What's at stake for Trump in Israel's deadlocked election?
summary: With Israel’s election yielding no clear winner, US President Donald Trump could face prolonged uncertainty over who will lead Washington’s closest Middle East ally as he confronts challenges from Iran and Gaza across the region.

While Netanyahu seemed in a stronger position, neither side was projected to have an outright path to form a new government after Israel’s first election since the Hamas-led attacks of Oct 7, 2023, and the ensuing wars in Gaza, Lebanon and Iran.

Trump has repeatedly signalled that the US and Israel could restart attacks on Iran after the midterms, with some critics, including in Israel, suggesting Netanyahu might see it as a way to bolster his political standing as caretaker prime minister.

stories.title: Netanyahu set to remain caretaker prime minister after inconclusive Israeli election
summary: Benjamin Netanyahu looked set to remain Israel’s caretaker prime minister after unexpectedly strong backing among Jewish voters left his opponents little apparent prospect of unseating him, despite his right-wing bloc losing its parliamentary majority.

With nearly 86 per cent of votes tallied on Wednesday, Israel’s three main broadcasters projected Netanyahu’s bloc of right-wing, far-right and ultra-Orthodox parties would win 53 seats in the 120-seat Knesset, well ahead of the 48 for rival Gadi Eisenkot’s opposition bloc.

But Yair Golan, the head of Israel’s main left-wing party, which is part of Eisenkot’s camp, called for precisely that on Wednesday. “We must no longer accept Netanyahu’s racist division between Jewish votes and Arab votes,” he said on X. “We have a responsibility.

stories.title: Israel's unassuming President Herzog holds keys to next government
summary: Israel’s President Isaac Herzog is known for his unassuming and mild manner, but all eyes will soon be on him as he decides who to task with forming the next coalition government.
In 2015, as leader of Israel’s centre-left Labour party, Herzog vied to oust Netanyahu as prime minister, presenting himself as a subdued, even-keeled alternative to the bombastic “Bibi”.

Herzog’s Irish-born father, Chaim Herzog, served as head of Israel’s military intelligence, then went on to become its ambassador to the United Nations and finally its sixth president, from 1983 to 1993.

stories.title: Noreen Niazi moved from Lahore jail to hospital due to high blood pressure: lawyer
summary: LAHORE: Incarcerated PTI founder Imran Khan’s sister Noreen Niazi was moved from Lahore’s Kot Lakhpat jail to the Punjab Institute of Cardiology on Wednesday due to high blood pressure, her lawyer said.

Three sisters of the ex-premier — Noreen, Aleema Khan, and Uzma Khan — have been detained since Sept 21 under the Punjab Maintenance of Public Order Ordinance, 1960 (MPO) on the Lahore deputy commissioner’s (DC) orders.
Noreen’s counsel Rana Mudassar Umer told Dawn that she had been taken to the Punjab Institute of Cardiology on the recommendation of the jail doctors.

stories.title: FCC expresses 'serious concern' over course adopted by SC bench over already-decided matter
summary: The two-judge SC bench had upheld that the Income Support Levy Act, having been enacted through the Finance Act 2013 without observance of the legislative procedure prescribed by the Constitution, did not acquire the status of a valid law.

In his judgment, the FCC chief justice also criticised the SC’s subsequent conduct by describing the development as an aspect of institutional significance concerning judicial discipline and consistency of judicial pronouncements.

Justice Aminuddin recalled that the constitutional validity of the Income Support Levy Act had already been examined by the two-judge SC bench in the ‘Commissioner Inland Revenue versus Muhammad Mustafa Gigi’ case in which the appeal was refused.

stories.title: Fazl accuses govt of 'misusing' Constitution when imposing emergency, governor's rule in KP
summary: ISLAMABAD: Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam—Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman on Wednesday accused the government of misusing the Constitution and resorting to unconstitutional measures in imposing governor’s rule and an emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
The Centre imposed governor’s rule and emergency in KP on Oct 11, citing the provincial government’s “deliberate disengagement” from the fight against terrorism.

The federal government on Oct 11 imposed an emergency and governor’s rule in KP under Articles 232 and 234 of the Constitution following the president’s approval of the recommendations by the federal cabinet.

stories.title: Two-day Sindh energy and climate moot announced
summary: Addressing a press conference at the Karachi Press Club, Climate Action Centre Director Yasir Darya said that Sindh, despite supplying electricity to a major part of the country, especially Punjab, did not have a proper energy policy of its own.

The event is being organised by Sath, the Climate Action Centre Karachi, the Civil Society Support Programme, the Pakistan Industrial Development Corporation, The Knowledge Forum, Indus Consortium and the Pakistan Research Institute for Energy and Development (PRIED).
On climate finance, he said there was a complaint that resources available to the Sindh government for climate action did not reach the city level, in Karachi or elsewhere in the province.

stories.title: Consignment of imported wheat arrives at Karachi port
summary: On Monday, Food Security Minister Rana Tanveer Hussain announced that the government would maintain strategic wheat reserves of up to six million tonnes.
The deputy prime minister “directed the concerned authorities to monitor market trends closely and ensure that the supply of wheat is adequate and atta prices are on a downward trajectory,” it added.
In a recent meeting, DPM Dar had directed federal and provincial governments to take all necessary measures, including increasing market supply, to bring wheat prices under control.

stories.title: Poverty climbs back to 28.9%
summary: "The political instability, policy discontinuity, economic crises and climate shocks reversed development gains," Iqbal said while speaking at an event organised to sign a memorandum of understanding with OPHI.

The minister, who has recently started speaking against the government's number-centric economic policies, emphasised the need for restoring social investment, empowering local governments and using poverty evidence to shape national development priorities.
Iqbal said political stability, sustained economic growth and continuity of national development priorities were essential to restoring poverty reduction.

stories.title: Insurance costs for maritime trade to fall
summary: He was addressing a symposium titled "Pakistan's Maritime Future: Maritime Security, Ocean Governance and Blue Economy", organised by the National Institute of Maritime Affairs.

The event brought together policymakers, academics and maritime officials to examine regional challenges, the evolving maritime order, emerging technologies, ocean governance and opportunities for ports and shipping sector to contribute to national security and economic growth.
Chaudhry said the Ministry of Maritime Affairs was working to improve port efficiency, expand the national merchant fleet, facilitate trade and attract investment.

stories.title: Three-year defect liability ordered
summary: He asked the relevant officials, Minister of State for Finance Bilal Azhar Kayani and representatives of the Constructors Association of Pakistan (CAP) to consult further on the proposed institutional structure.

CAP proposed applying it to projects valued at Rs20 billion and above, while the minister called for the threshold to be lowered and for further consultation among stakeholders to determine an appropriate limit.

The meeting was attended by Minister of State for Finance Bilal Azhar Kayani, Housing Secretary Captain (retd) Muhammad Mahmood, a member of the Planning Commission, the PPRA managing director, representatives of CAP and other senior officials.

stories.title: Gold jumps ahead of US Fed policy decision
summary: Gold prices in Pakistan increased by Rs3,500 per tola on Wednesday, despite a slight decline in international market, as investors awaited the US Federal Reserve's monetary policy decision and comments from its chair for clues about the future path of rates.
In the local market, gold prices rose to Rs425,636 per tola, according to rates released by the All-Pakistan Gems and Jewellers Sarafa Association (APGJSA).

Internationally, the US dollar held near two-week highs ahead of central bank policy decisions, with the Federal Reserve widely expected to keep rates unchanged while signalling the possibility of a move in December.

stories.title: 'More rate hikes may follow'
summary: He expects monetary policy to remain tight, with rate cuts unlikely unless energy prices stabilise and inflation records a sustained decline.
Looking ahead, he expects inflation to remain elevated and volatile if global energy prices and domestic food supply pressures persist.
Persistent inflation and uncertainty over global energy prices could keep the policy rate elevated, but the cost of credit may restrict business investment and weigh on economic activity.

stories.title: PSX climbs 1,270 points as policy fears ease
summary: Investors came back and buying gathered pace late in the session, which helped the KSE-100 index close with notable gains of 1,269.55 points, or 0.77%, at 165,736.76.
Ahmed Sheraz, equity trader at KASB KTrade, noted that the KSE-100 closed with an increase of 1,270 points (+0.77%) in a broadly positive session, with approximately 183 million shares traded.

Topline Securities observed that the benchmark index maintained a positive trajectory throughout the session, touching the intra-day high of 1,633 points, while the downside remained limited to 111 points, reflecting sustained buying interest and improved investor sentiment.

stories.title: Pakistan terms Afghan claims regarding Angoor Adda incident 'fabrication of lies'
summary: It was also reported that the Afghan Taliban engaged in unprovoked firing the night before near Kurram as security forces foiled an attempt by terrorists to cross into Pakistan.
Around mid-October, the state media reported that security forces had again responded to unprovoked firing by Afghan Taliban forces along the Pakistan-Afghanistan border in KP’s Upper Kurram.
It quoted security sources as saying that several personnel of the Afghan Taliban were “reportedly killed during the Pakistan Army’s retaliatory action along the Ghuzgarhi border”.

stories.title: World Bank rates progress on KP hydropower, renewable energy project 'moderately unsatisfactory'
summary: In its public disclosure, the Washington-based lending agency rated the progress towards the achievement of project development objectives as “moderately unsatisfactory”.
However, the World Bank rated the overall implementation progress as “moderately satisfactory” and described the overall risk rating as “substantial”.

The KP Hydropower and Renewable Energy Development project was conceived as a transformational programme to help build capacity and institutions for harvesting the vast renewable energy potential in the province.

stories.title: Govt considering creation of regulatory authority for construction industry
summary: ISLAMABAD: The government is considering establishing two new bodies — a regulatory authority and a marketing entity — for the construction industry along with a three-year defect liability period for major construction projects in the country.

Private sector figures in construction and the government, however, differ over the financial size for the application of a defect liability period, with the construction industry seeking a minimum threshold of Rs20 billion and the government pushing for lower amounts.

These issues were discussed at an exploratory meeting, chaired by Economic Affairs Minister Ahad Cheema, on introducing reforms for the country’s construction sector, improving project delivery and addressing key issues faced by the industry.

stories.title: Haris Rauf penalised for breach of ICC Code of Conduct in tri-series match against England
summary: Pakistan pacer Haris Rauf has been fined 20pc of his match-fee for breaching the International Cricket Council (ICC) Code of Conduct during the One-day International (ODI) tri-series match against England on Sunday.

According to an ICC media released issued on Wednesday, Haris was found to be in breach of Level 1 of the code for appealing for a wide from the n0n-striker’s end in the 46th over and argued with England all-rounder Will Jacks after it was denied.
Haris hit the winning run at the end of an 89-run partnership with Shadab to propel Pakistan into the series final, after the home side were reduced to 154-9 in pursuit of England’s 242.

stories.title: Filing your tax return on IRIS: A step-by-step guide for the salaried individual
summary: Your employer pays the tax, but only you can file the return.
Enter the CPR number in your return so IRIS knows the tax has been paid.
Myth: “My income is too low to bother.”Reality: Filing a return showing zero tax still makes you a filer, and that saves you money elsewhere.

stories.title: Secret to country's development lies in AI and digitisation, PM Shehbaz stresses
summary: The prime minister directed that an AI-assisted cancer early-detection system be implemented at the earliest in collaboration with Alibaba.

The prime minister directed all relevant authorities to ensure that cooperation with Alibaba was translated into tangible results through clearly defined targets, timelines and effective monitoring of all projects.

Meanwhile, a two-year programme is being launched through collaboration between the Small and Medium Enterprises Development Authority (Smeda) and Alibaba to provide SMEs with access to international markets, training and e-commerce opportunities.

stories.title: Austria to launch parliamentary inquiry into use of smart glasses amid privacy concerns
summary: Alexander Proll presented a three-stage model aimed at regulating smart glasses, which can feature built-in cameras, microphones and artificial intelligence functions, public broadcaster ORF reported.

Proll said a parliamentary inquiry would be the next step, bringing together experts in science, data protection and technology, as well as representatives of people affected by the use of smart glasses.
Meanwhile, nearly 25,000 people have signed a petition calling for a ban on smart glasses, according to ORF.

stories.title: Pakistan allows Taiwanese airlines to use airspace till March 2027
summary: Meanwhile, the report also cited flight-tracking data, which said that Taiwanese carriers began rerouting flights over the weekend, with both airlines no longer flying over Pakistan since the morning of Oct 25.

Taiwanese airlines had avoided Russian airspace since February 2022, in line with many Asian, European and North American carriers, although they were never formally barred from using it, the report said.
Note: This story earlier stated that Pakistan had barred Taiwanese airlines from using its airspace due to Beijing’s One-China policy.

stories.title: US tech giant Google unveils Gemini 4 Carbon AI model
summary: Google announced its latest artificial intelligence (AI) model, Gemini 4 Carbon, on Wednesday, claiming significant gains in coding, autonomous agent tasks and cybersecurity defence.

Unveiled just two weeks after launching its Gemini 4 Argon model, the company described Carbon in a blog post as its strongest frontier model, with state-of-the-art cybersecurity and long-horizon capabilities.

It’s rolling out starting… pic.twitter.com/oQrHzxvMSo — Google (@Google) October 28, 2026 The company claimed that Gemini 4 Carbon ranks first on the updated version 5.0 of the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index with a score of 59.

stories.title: ‘God will surely provide’: Afghans compete for jobs, homes as millions return from neighbouring countries
summary: As labourers gathered at a roadside in northern Afghanistan, Ghulam Sakhi Barat joined the search for work, with millions of new arrivals intensifying pressure for jobs and homes.

More than six million Afghans have returned from Iran and Pakistan in little over three years as the neighbouring countries have launched deportation drives after decades hosting those fleeing conflict.
Competition for housing is fierce, with residents who spoke to AFP reporting rent surging by as much as 150 percent in recent years.

stories.title: Govt directs preparation of 5-year roadmap to boost kinnow exports
summary: Dr Bharath directed the Pakistan Horticulture Development and Export Company to prepare a five-year roadmap within 15 days for increasing exports and promoting value addition of kinnow and other citrus fruits.
Last year, the government announced a set of measures aimed at enhancing the global recognition of Pakistani kinnow, with a focus on improving its export potential and value-added products.

These included promoting seedless kinnow, value-added citrus products such as juices, concentrates, and essential oils, capacity building for growers and exporters, as well as registration of new exporters for markets like Uzbekistan and other Central Asian countries.

stories.title: 'Conscience does not permit': LHC's Justice Kayani resigns, cites 'executive's growing control' over judiciary
summary: Justice Kayani previously served as the senior puisne judge of the IHC and was expecting to be elevated to the post of the high court’s chief justice.

However, the transfer of incumbent IHC Chief Justice Sardar Muhammad Sarfraz Dogar from the LHC, along with two other judges from the Sindh and Balochistan high courts, prompted him to challenge the inter-high court transfers.
Justice Kayani and other senior IHC judges approached the Supreme Court to challenge the administrative powers exercised by Chief Justice Dogar.

stories.title: At least 64 people killed in Spain as two high-speed trains collide
summary: The accident comes after a collision between two high-speed trains in southern Spain in January resulted in the deaths of 46 people.

PM Sanchez, who is seeking re-election next month, said he was “shocked” by the incident. “Shocked by the serious train accident in Toledo,” Sanchez said on X about the incident south of Madrid, sending “my love, solidarity and support to all the victims and their families”.

PM Shehbaz Sharif said he was “profoundly grieved by the devastating train collision” and expressed his deepest condolences to Sanchez and the people of Spain. “We pray for the speedy recovery of the injured.

stories.title: 'Nobody heard us' – why Gen Z are leading protests across Europe
summary: Thousands of young people marched through the streets of several Italian cities, including Milan and Rome.
The protests encompassed a broad range of issues from education and corruption to anti-war movements and rising costs.
The protests are still spreading, with a demonstration planned in Germany this weekend over the cost of living, inequality, war and the state of schools.

stories.title: Govt increases petrol by Rs1.85, diesel by Rs1.75 for Oct 29
summary: According to a notification issued by the Petroleum Division, the price of petrol was fixed at Rs377.91 per litre, while HSD would cost Rs399.82 per litre on Thursday.

On September 13, PM Shehbaz announced a special relief scheme offering Rs100 per litre off petrol for motorcycles, three-wheeler rickshaws and cars with engines up to 800cc, in an attempt to shield lower-income consumers from the impact of rising petroleum prices.
Oil prices climbed about 2% on ‌Wednesday as continued fighting in Yemen and an attack on a refinery in Saudi Arabia renewed concerns about additional supply disruptions from the Middle East.

stories.title: ECP orders immediate local body polls in KP districts demarcated, sans those under ARDC
summary: ISLAMABAD: The Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) on Wednesday ordered local government (LG) elections to be held immediately in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa districts where delimitation had been completed, excluding those included in the 12 districts with special emergency measures.

A day earlier, the ECP had reserved the verdict after hearing the provincial government’s request to defer local government elections, citing law and order, the imposition of emergency and deployment of troops under Article 245.

In its order, issued on Wednesday and seen by Dawn, the ECP directed its office to submit the election programme for its approval in respect of districts where the delimitation process had been completed.

stories.title: Michigan Senate race a test of attacks on Muslim candidate, progressive agenda
summary: The race has been defined by anti-Muslim rhetoric, including from US… pic.twitter.com/uuR13yfoJ9 — FRANCE 24 English (@France24_en) October 27, 2026 Trump has falsely accused El-Sayed of ​being a Muslim extremist, while Rogers has tried to tie him to the Muslim Brotherhood.

"He's a Muslim-American, and so Rogers is attempting to do his best to portray El-Sayed ​as an outsider who's dangerous," said Jonathan Hanson, a political scientist and public policy lecturer at the University of Michigan.

Rogers has based that claim in part on a 2012 group letter signed by El-Sayed and other Egyptian Americans in support of then-newly elected Egyptian President Mohamed Morsi, who was backed by the Muslim Brotherhood.

stories.title: Imaan, Hadi allege security breach case 'nothing more than harassment' for their human rights work
summary: Imaan and Hadi are facing a jail trial in a 2024 case on the alleged disruption of an international cricket team’s security route and incitement to public unrest.
Imaan pointed out that the entire jail trial had been challenged by the couple in the Islamabad High Court (IHC) as well as the Supreme Court (SC).

Jailed, sentenced, re-arrested The couple has been in jail since their arrest on Jan 23 in a case registered against them for protesting outside the IHC and allegedly manhandling the IHC Bar Association president.

stories.title: Imran Khan’s sister Noreen taken to Punjab Institute of Cardiology after health issue in jail: lawyer
summary: Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) founder Imran Khan’s sister Noreen Niazi, 70, was admitted to Lahore's Punjab Institute of Cardiology (PIC) on Wednesday following a deterioration in her health while in custody, according to her legal counsel.

The detention at Kot Lakhpat Jail was later extended on October 7 for another 30 days. “Noreen Niazi Sahiba has been transferred to Punjab Institute of Cardiology due to deteriorating health in jail,” her legal counsel, Rana Mudassar Umer, said on X.

Two days earlier on October 26, the Lahore High Court disposed of a petition for the release of Imran’s three sisters after the Punjab government confirmed that their detention had been extended by another 30 days. ---------------------- More to follow.

stories.title: Iran's Revolutionary Court sentences director Panahi to jail term, travel ban
summary: Iran's Revolutionary Court sentenced award-winning film director Jafar ​Panahi to five years in ‌prison and the seizure of all his assets, Iran's semi-official Nournews ​reported on Wednesday, citing ​his lawyer but without mentioning the ⁠charges he faced.
The court ​also banned Panahi from leaving the ​country for two years and from any social media activity, the report ​said.
Despite having been sentenced to a one-year prison sentence in absentia in 2025 for propaganda activities against the system, Panahi returned to the country in March.

stories.title: US costs of Iran war rise to over $47bn, according to Pentagon estimate
summary: The US military has spent over $47 billion so far to prosecute the war in Iran, more than 25 per cent higher than the Defense Department’s estimate in July, according to Pentagon data obtained by Reuters.
The Pentagon’s latest estimate was tied to the operational costs of carrying out the war, with a projected cost of more than $29 billion to replace expended munitions used in the conflict.
The latest Pentagon estimate compares to Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth’s July estimate of $37.5 billion for the cost of the war.

stories.title: Muslims in Texas seek greater political influence ahead of US midterm elections
summary: The dispute has become one example of a broader question facing Muslim Americans: can greater political organisation help them influence public policy and counter discrimination?

Yet a growing political presence does not necessarily translate into electoral power, nor are Muslim Americans a unified voting bloc: their party affiliations, social views and policy priorities vary considerably.
Hassan’s approach reflects one strand of Muslim political activism: using elections and party organisations to defend civil rights and influence decisions affecting the community.

stories.title: Religious scholars reaffirm fatwa against suicide attacks, terrorism
summary: Religious scholars, spiritual leaders and representatives of different faiths unanimously reaffirmed the fatwa (religious ruling) against suicide attacks, terrorism, extremism and the killing of innocent people, while fully endorsing the national narrative of Paigham-e-Pakistan.

The participants also expressed full support for the efforts of the Pakistan Army and national security institutions against what the declaration described as Fitna al-Khawarij and Fitna al-Hindustan.

stories.title: Bulk carrier docks at Karachi port with 51,000 metric tonnes of wheat
summary: According to a statement issued after the meeting, FM Dar emphasised that maintaining adequate wheat stocks and preventing disruptions in the supply of grain remained among the government’s top priorities.
The deputy prime minister directed the relevant authorities to closely monitor market trends and ensure adequate wheat supplies across Pakistan.
Deputy Prime Minister/Foreign Minister Senator Mohammad Ishaq Dar @MIshaqDar50 chaired a meeting of the Steering Committee on Wheat today.

stories.title: PTI decides to contest Islamabad local bodies elections on Dec 20
summary: On Wednesday, PTI’s Islamabad wing President Amir Mughal, speaking to Dawn, said, “We have decided to contest elections on all 125 seats of union councils”.

Mughal said that PTI visited areas across the city to get input from the people, claiming that “over 95 per cent of people suggested contesting the elections.” “They were of the view that the government can not do more than what it is already doing with the party.

Claiming that Islamabad had traditionally been a PTI stronghold, the party expressed confidence it would secure a sweeping victory in the local government elections, similar to the result it claimed to have achieved in the 2024 General Elections.
